description: We’re a group of curious, adventurous girls who love discovering new things and taking on exciting challenges! Whether it’s trying a new hobby, exploring unfamiliar places, learning a new skill, or stepping out of our comfort zones, we’re always up for the next adventure. Here, every day is a chance to learn, grow, and have fun together. We cheer each other on, celebrate every win (big or small), and believe that the best memories are made when we dare to try something new. Ready to join the adventure? Come explore with us!
summary:
Junior Astronaut is a 2D educational game that transforms space exploration into an interactive adventure for young students. With a simple and accessible interface, it introduces STEM concepts — Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics — in a child-friendly way.
Players solve a riddle, identify their astronaut, and choose their mission destination: the Moon or Mars. They then customize their spaceship with colors, stickers, and a name, select their spacesuit, and choose the essential supplies for the journey. These activities encourage creativity, planning, and an understanding of the resources and equipment required for space missions.
Throughout the adventure, players complete interactive activities, including planetary memory games, ordering planets according to their distance from the Sun, and quizzes. Earned coins can be spent at the space shop to purchase essential items for the return journey. The game also features map navigation to a space museum, where players can complete another quiz and finish their experience.
According to the project description, the quizzes and survival parameters for the Moon and Mars were developed using official NASA datasets and educational materials. By combining exploration, challenges, problem-solving, and decision-making, Junior Astronaut presents scientific concepts in a playful and intuitive way, sparking curiosity and encouraging interest in science and space exploration.
details:
Junior Astronaut is an interactive 2D educational game designed to introduce children aged 7 to 12 to space exploration and STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics) through an engaging, hands-on learning experience. The project transforms scientific concepts into a space adventure in which players become astronauts, make decisions, solve challenges, and learn while progressing through a mission.

What does the project do and how does it work?

The game takes players through a complete space mission, from preparing a spacecraft to returning to Earth and completing a visit to a Space Museum.

The adventure begins with a challenge: players must solve a riddle to unlock the spacecraft and identify themselves as astronauts. They then access the control panel and choose their destination: the Moon or Mars. The game introduces information about the average distance to each destination and the approximate travel time, helping children compare different space journeys.

Before departure, players personalize their spacecraft by selecting colors, decorations, and a name. They also choose an astronaut suit and decide which supplies to take on the mission. These activities encourage creativity while introducing the importance of planning and preparation for space exploration.

After launch, players complete educational activities, including planet memory games and challenges involving the correct order of the planets from the Sun. They earn coins as they progress and must manage these resources in a space shop, purchasing the supplies needed for the return journey. This introduces basic financial decision-making, resource management, and problem-solving.

The adventure continues with a navigation challenge in which players follow a map to reach the Space Museum. There, they take a final quiz to demonstrate what they have learned and complete their journey by receiving a certificate.

What are the benefits of the project?

Junior Astronaut combines entertainment and education to make scientific learning more accessible and meaningful. Its main benefits include:

  • STEM learning: introduces astronomy, planetary science, mathematics, and concepts related to space exploration.
  • Active learning: encourages children to learn by solving problems, answering questions, and completing interactive challenges.
  • Critical thinking: requires players to interpret information, make choices, and find solutions.
  • Decision-making and resource management: encourages players to plan their missions and use limited coins to obtain essential supplies.
  • Scientific curiosity: inspires children to explore the universe and ask questions about the Moon, Mars, planets, and the challenges of space travel.
  • Engagement with technology: provides an opportunity to interact with a digital educational environment and develop confidence in learning through games.

What is the intended impact of the project?

The main goal is to stimulate children's interest in science and space exploration from an early age. By presenting scientific knowledge through an adventure, the project aims to reduce the distance between complex scientific subjects and young learners.

Junior Astronaut seeks to show children that science is not limited to textbooks or classrooms: it can be explored through curiosity, experimentation, challenges, and play. It also aims to encourage children to imagine themselves as future scientists, engineers, researchers, and astronauts.

The project is intended to support teachers and families as an educational resource that can complement science lessons, encourage collaborative learning, and create opportunities for conversations about space exploration and the importance of scientific research.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software were used?

The game was developed with the support of Google AI Studio, used as an AI-assisted development environment to help create and structure the interactive experience. It was designed as a browser-based 2D game and published through Netlify, making it accessible through a public web link without requiring players to download or install a separate application.

The educational content and scientific parameters were informed by datasets and official materials from NASA, connecting the game to real scientific information and space research.

No specialized hardware is required. Players need an internet-connected device and a compatible web browser.

How is the project creative?

The creativity of Junior Astronaut lies in combining several educational approaches into one continuous space adventure. Instead of presenting isolated questions or facts, the game places children in the role of astronauts who must make decisions and take responsibility for the progress of their mission.

Its creative approach includes:

  • Learning through storytelling: scientific activities are connected by a mission with a clear beginning, progression, and conclusion.
  • Personalization: players create their own spacecraft, choose its appearance, and give it a name, building a stronger connection with the experience.
  • Gamification: points, coins, quizzes, memory games, and certificates transform learning objectives into motivating challenges.
  • Learning through consequences: players must consider their choices, particularly when selecting supplies and managing resources for the journey home.
  • A combination of subjects: astronomy, mathematics, logical reasoning, navigation, and decision-making appear together in a single educational experience.
  • Real science in a playful environment: NASA-related scientific information provides a connection between the fictional adventure and real space exploration.

What factors did the team consider?

The project was designed around the needs and interests of children aged 7 to 12. The team considered age-appropriate language, accessible challenges, intuitive interactions, visual engagement, and a gradual progression from simpler activities to more demanding decisions.

Another important consideration was balancing entertainment with educational value. Each stage was designed to have a learning purpose, so that players would not simply collect points but also develop knowledge and skills throughout the mission.

The team also considered accessibility and ease of distribution. Making the game available through a web link removes the need for installation and makes it easier for families, teachers, and students to access the experience.

Ultimately, Junior Astronaut was created with one central idea: every child should have the opportunity to explore the universe, discover science, and imagine a future among the stars.
